---
title: "Errata"
subtitle: "On Coppock and Kaur (2022), *American Journal of Political Science* 66(3)"
format:
  pdf:
    output-file: coppock_kaur_2022_errata.pdf
    geometry: margin=1.25in
    fontsize: 11pt
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        \usepackage{caption}
        \captionsetup{labelformat=empty}
        \usepackage{float}
        \floatplacement{table}{H}
        \floatplacement{figure}{H}
---

The maintained replication code behind these errata is at <https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_kaur_2022> and is archived at Zenodo at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168367>, a DOI that always resolves to the latest version.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

out <- function(file) read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output", file), show_col_types = FALSE)

table_3 <- out("table_3_toy_example.csv")
table_4 <- out("table_4_probabilistic.csv")
summary_stats <- out("text_summary_stats.csv")
imputation_counts <- out("text_imputation_counts.csv")
corrections <- out("appendix_c_corrections.csv")
table_b2_corrected <- out("table_b2_corrected_rows.csv")
expected_bounds <- out("text_expected_bounds.csv")

# The two appendix Table B.2 cells that disagree with the case file behind them. Both sides
# are read rather than typed: the published side from the transcription of the appendix, the
# corrected side from the deposited case file the rest of the table reproduces exactly.
appendix_published <- read_csv(
  here::here("ground_truth", "published_appendix_values.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

appendix_pair <- appendix_published |>
  inner_join(out("table_b1_b2_case_dataset.csv"), by = c("table", "case"),
             suffix = c("_published", "_rewrite"))

# fixed(), because a case label carries its years in parentheses and str_starts reads its
# pattern as a regex: "Burundi (1996" is an unterminated group.
azerbaijan <- appendix_pair |> filter(str_starts(case, fixed("Azerbaijan")), table == "B.2")
burundi <- appendix_pair |> filter(str_starts(case, fixed("Burundi (1996")), table == "B.2")
stopifnot(nrow(azerbaijan) == 1, nrow(burundi) == 1,
          azerbaijan$Y_published != azerbaijan$Y_rewrite,
          burundi$probability_published != burundi$probability_rewrite)

# The two revealed untreated outcomes transposed between Azerbaijan and Bangladesh. The
# published side is the transcription of the appendix, which prints the deposit; the
# corrected side is the value apply_appendix_c_corrections.R restores. The swap is what
# leaves every bound where it was, so the gate checks it rather than the prose asserting it.
revealed <- out("revealed_outcome_corrections.csv") |>
  mutate(case = str_c(location, " (", conflict_start, "-", conflict_end, ")")) |>
  left_join(appendix_pair |> filter(table == "B.2") |>
              select(case, observed_published, imputed_y0_published),
            by = "case", relationship = "one-to-one")
revealed_az <- revealed |> filter(location == "Azerbaijan")
revealed_bd <- revealed |> filter(location == "Bangladesh")
stopifnot(nrow(revealed_az) == 1, nrow(revealed_bd) == 1,
          all(revealed$observed_published == revealed$deposited_y0),
          all(as.numeric(revealed$imputed_y0_published) == revealed$deposited_y0),
          sum(revealed$corrected_y0) == sum(revealed$deposited_y0))

fmt0 <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f", x)
fmt1 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)

# The published side of every entry is transcribed from the article, never
# computed. value_paper is a string by rule: read as a number, "0.20" and ".2"
# stop being distinguishable from what the page prints.
published_claims <- read_csv(
  here::here("ground_truth", "published_claims.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(value_paper = col_character(), .default = col_character())
)

published_value <- function(id) {
  hit <- published_claims$value_paper[published_claims$claim_id == id]
  stopifnot(length(hit) == 1, !is.na(hit))
  hit
}

summary_value <- function(which_claim) {
  hit <- summary_stats$value[summary_stats$claim == which_claim]
  stopifnot(length(hit) == 1)
  hit
}

count_value <- function(sample, quantity_label) {
  hit <- imputation_counts$value[imputation_counts$transition_fac == sample &
                                   imputation_counts$quantity == quantity_label]
  stopifnot(length(hit) == 1)
  hit
}

# A plotted bound, at its exact value. The bounds are affine in the imputed
# potential outcomes, so the distribution the deposited script samples from is
# available in closed form, and the maintained figures enumerate it rather than
# drawing from it. Every corrected bound below is therefore an exact value and
# not one draw of an unseeded simulation.
exact_bound <- function(sample, which_estimand, which_step, side) {
  row <- expected_bounds |>
    filter(transition_fac == sample, estimand == which_estimand, step == which_step)
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1)
  row[[str_c("expected_", side)]]
}

# Two of the corrected values replace a number the article spells out, so they are
# spelled out too rather than printed as digits: the correction is one token. The
# counts in the prose and the headings use it for the same reason, and because a
# count typed into a document about miscounted numbers is the obvious place for
# this document to go stale.
english_number <- function(x) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten",
             "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen", "seventeen",
             "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty", "twenty-one", "twenty-two", "twenty-three",
             "twenty-four", "twenty-five")
  stopifnot(x >= 1, x <= length(words), x == round(x))
  words[x]
}

# A probability the article prints without a trailing zero, as its tables do.
probability_string <- function(x) format(x, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE)

treated_ones <- sum(table_3$d == 1 & table_3$Y == 1)
unit_6_probability <- sum(table_4$prob[table_4$unit_6 == 1])
unit_7_probability <- sum(table_4$prob[table_4$unit_7 == 1])
disbanded_cases <- count_value("Democratization", "cases at step: Disbanded and Discredited Cases")
treated_cases <- count_value("Democratization", "treated")

complemented <- corrections |>
  filter(near(deposited_probability + appendix_c_probability, 1))
off_by_one_step <- corrections |>
  filter(!near(deposited_probability + appendix_c_probability, 1))

att_exact <- exact_bound("Democratization", "ATT", "s4", "lower")
att_published <- published_value("figure_3|low_bound_att_unimputable_cases")

# Widths are differences of two exact bounds rather than of two draws, for the
# same reason the bounds themselves are.
atu_width_exact <- exact_bound("Democratization", "ATU", "s4", "upper") -
  exact_bound("Democratization", "ATU", "s4", "lower")
ate_width_exact <- exact_bound("Democratization", "ATE", "s4", "upper") -
  exact_bound("Democratization", "ATE", "s4", "lower")
eoc_initial_width_exact <- exact_bound("End of conflict", "ATE", "obs", "upper") -
  exact_bound("End of conflict", "ATE", "obs", "lower")
eoc_final_width_exact <- exact_bound("End of conflict", "ATE", "s4", "upper") -
  exact_bound("End of conflict", "ATE", "s4", "lower")

# What the deposited script's method gives for the same four bounds, which is a
# different pair of whole numbers depending on the seed it is run at. The
# democratization ATT sits exactly on a rounding boundary, so the two whole
# numbers either side of it come up about equally often.
att_drawn_labels <- read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output", "text_seed_sensitivity.csv"),
                             show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  count(dem_att_label) |>
  arrange(desc(n))

# The published figure labels beside the corrected expectations, for the two
# floats whose labels move. The description is the step label the figure prints.
label_table <- function(float, which_estimand, sample, id_infix) {
  steps <- tibble(
    step = c("agnostic", "obs", "s0", "s1", "s2", "s3", "s4"),
    description = c("Before Any Data", "Initial Values",
                    "Disbanded and Discredited Cases", "Treated Cases",
                    "Non-transitional Cases", "Untreated Cases", "Unimputable Cases"),
    slug = c("before_any_data", "initial_values", "disbanded_and_discredited_cases",
             "treated_cases", "non_transitional_cases", "untreated_cases",
             "unimputable_cases")
  )
  steps |>
    mutate(
      published = str_c("[", map_chr(str_c(float, "|low_bound_", id_infix, slug), published_value),
                        ", ", map_chr(str_c(float, "|high_bound_", id_infix, slug), published_value),
                        "]"),
      corrected = str_c(
        "[", sprintf("%.1f", map_dbl(step, \(s) exact_bound(sample, which_estimand, s, "lower"))),
        ", ", sprintf("%.1f", map_dbl(step, \(s) exact_bound(sample, which_estimand, s, "upper"))),
        "]"
      ),
      moved = published != str_c("[", sprintf("%.0f", map_dbl(step, \(s) exact_bound(sample, which_estimand, s, "lower"))),
                                 ", ", sprintf("%.0f", map_dbl(step, \(s) exact_bound(sample, which_estimand, s, "upper"))), "]"),
      corrected = if_else(moved, str_c("\\textbf{", corrected, "}"), corrected)
    ) |>
    select(Step = description, Published = published, Corrected = corrected)
}
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here, \was{} in an edition. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be
# set by either. Four of these entries correct a float rather than a sentence, and there the
# published and corrected fields name what moves while the corrected float is reprinted
# beneath: floats are presentation, not spine.
#
# Numbering follows PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b: entries are ordered by severity block (quantity;
# description, interpretation, definition; label, float, cross_reference; wording, spelling,
# typography; bibliographic), discovery order inside a block, and a finding that lands in an
# earlier block renumbers the entries after it. Renumbered 2026-11-07; the old-to-new map is
# in that day's commit message.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated, so that
# "is this finding published?" is a query rather than a judgment. Entries 1 and 2 carry
# none: they are the transcription errors that CAUSE the four below them, and the ground
# truth summarises appendix Table B.2 one column at a time rather than one cell at a time,
# so no row states an individual imputation probability. Every id here is checked against
# the ground truth by build_ground_truth.R.
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, on the
# claim's scale, carrying the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. Each
# value is computed once, here, and the corrected sentence below is glued from the same
# object, so the two cannot be written apart; the gate after the spine re-checks that each
# value sits inside the [[...]] span it belongs to. An entry of a class that changes no
# quantity, a note-form entry, and an entry with no claim_ids carry NA.
cv3 <- sprintf('%.1f', att_exact)
cv6 <- c(sprintf('%.0f', count_value('Democratization', 'imputed_with_certainty')),
         sprintf('%.0f', count_value('Democratization', 'imputed_probabilistically')))
cv7 <- treated_ones
cv8 <- c(sprintf('%.1f', unit_6_probability), sprintf('%.1f', unit_7_probability))
cv9 <- sprintf('%.1f', eoc_final_width_exact)
cv10 <- disbanded_cases

entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "brief",
  str_glue("{str_to_sentence(english_number(nrow(complemented)))} imputation probabilities carried as their complements"),
  "app. Table B.2",
  str_glue("[[{english_number(nrow(complemented))} imputation probabilities in appendix Table B.2, each one minus the probability the appendix C entry for that case states]]"),
  "[[the probabilities appendix C states]]",
  str_glue(
    "In all {english_number(nrow(complemented))} the deposit contradicts itself, because an ",
    "imputed potential outcome of 1 sits beside a probability below one half. Appendix Table ",
    "B.2 prints the deposited value, so the published table inherits the transcription error ",
    "rather than committing a second one. Section C.2.7 reads \"we imputed that ",
    "$\\tilde{{Y}}_i(0) = 1$, with a probability of 0.8\" for South Africa, and the main text ",
    "says the same thing on page 10: \"In other words, $Y_i(0) = 1$ with a probability of ",
    ".8.\" Sections C.4.12 and C.4.13 read \"with a probability of 0.7.\""),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "brief",
  str_glue("{str_to_sentence(english_number(nrow(off_by_one_step)))} imputation probabilities differing by one step"),
  "app. Table B.2",
  str_glue("[[{english_number(nrow(off_by_one_step))} imputation probabilities in appendix Table B.2, each differing from the probability appendix C states by 0.1]]"),
  "[[the probabilities appendix C states]]",
  str_glue(
    "Uruguay is the one of the {english_number(nrow(off_by_one_step))} that matters beyond ",
    "the table: at the deposited 1 it is an imputation made with certainty, and at the 0.9 ",
    "appendix C states it is a probabilistic one. That is what entry 4 below turns on."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  3, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The average treatment effect on the treated",
  "*Imputing Missing Potential Outcomes*, Summary",
  str_glue("The bounds on the ATU are greater than 58 points wide, compared with the bounds on the ATT, which shrink all the way down to a point. We can summarize the ATT as a [[{att_published}]] percentage point effect on return to authoritarianism."),
  str_glue("The bounds on the ATU are greater than 58 points wide, compared with the bounds on the ATT, which shrink all the way down to a point. We can summarize the ATT as a [[{cv3}]] percentage point effect on return to authoritarianism."),
  str_glue(
    "Every treated case has both potential outcomes filled in by the second imputation step, ",
    "which is why the ATT bounds collapse to a point, and that point is the mean of the ",
    "eight observed treated outcomes minus the mean of the eight imputed untreated ones. ",
    "South Africa is one of the eight, so restoring its probability from 0.2 to the 0.8 ",
    "appendix C states moves the ATT by ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', abs(att_exact - as.numeric(att_published)))} points. The ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', att_exact)} is exact and not a draw: with both potential outcomes of ",
    "all {english_number(treated_cases)} treated cases imputed, the bound is a fixed ",
    "function of the imputation probabilities, and this is its value. It falls exactly ",
    "halfway between two whole numbers, so a whole-number restatement of the sentence would ",
    "not be determined, which is a further reason to correct it at one decimal as this ",
    "document corrects every percentage-point quantity. The ATU claim in the first clause is ",
    "unaffected and is left at the precision the article states it: the width is ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', atu_width_exact)} points before the correction and after it, because ",
    "both ATU bounds move by the same amount, so the published \"greater than ",
    "{published_value('text|atu_final_bounds_width')}\" holds exactly as written and is not ",
    "restated at one decimal here."),
  "text|att_summarised_as_a_point_effect",
  cv3,

  4, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "How the 63 missing potential outcomes were imputed",
  "*Imputing Missing Potential Outcomes*",
  "For all 63 unobserved potential outcomes, we imputed [[5]] with certainty, [[26]] probabilistically and we left 32 unimputed.",
  str_glue("For all 63 unobserved potential outcomes, we imputed [[{cv6[1]}]] with certainty, [[{cv6[2]}]] probabilistically and we left 32 unimputed."),
  paste(

  str_c("text|unobserved_potential_outcomes_imputed_with_certainty;",
        "text|unobserved_potential_outcomes_imputed_probabilistically"),
  str_c(cv6, collapse = ";"),

  5, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The toy example's treated outcomes",
  "*A Toy Example*",
  "The outcome for [[three]] of the treated units and one of the untreated units is 1; the outcome is equal to 0 for the remaining units.",
  str_glue("The outcome for [[{english_number(cv7)}]] of the treated units and one of the untreated units is 1; the outcome is equal to 0 for the remaining units."),
  str_glue(

  str_glue("Instead of being sure that the untreated potential outcomes for units 6 and 7 are 0, we think the probabilities of being a `1' for units 6 and 7 are [[{cv8[1]} and {cv8[2]}]], respectively ($k = 2$)."),
  str_glue(

  7, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",

  str_glue(

  "A list that ends without a full stop",
  "app. p. 19, Section C.5",
  "Niger (1974-1991), Zambia [[(1967-1991)]]",
  "Niger (1974-1991), Zambia [[(1967-1991).]]",
  "The paragraph listing the cases left unimputed ends with the last of them and no full stop.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  16, "bibliographic", "reading", "brief",
  "An author list that begins with \"et al\"",
  "p. 695, refs",
  "[[et al Mombauer, Annika.]] 2013.",
  "[[Mombauer, Annika.]] 2013.",
  str_c("The entry is alphabetized under M, so the \"et al\" is not the publisher reading a ",
        "coauthor into the citation: the article Mombauer wrote has none."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  17, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "A page range whose last page belongs to another article",
  "p. 695, refs",
  "48(2): 231–[[417]].",
  "48(2): 231–[[40]].",
  str_c("Mombauer's article runs from 231 to 240 (doi ",
        "[10.1177/0022009412472712](https://doi.org/10.1177/0022009412472712))."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  18, "bibliographic", "reading", "brief",
  "A multiplication sign printed as an italic X",
  "p. 695, refs",
  "Causal Effects from [[2X 2]] Tables",
  "Causal Effects from [[2 $\\times$ 2]] Tables",
  str_c("Keele and Quinn's title is \"Bayesian sensitivity analysis for causal effects from ",
        "$2 \\times 2$ tables ...\" (doi ",
        "[10.1214/17-AOAS1048](https://doi.org/10.1214/17-AOAS1048)). The published page sets ",
        "the multiplication sign as a math italic X with no space around it."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  # Entries 19 to 21 come from the reference audit's re-run of 2026-10-29, which learned to
  # read a page range printed as its first page alone. Each corrected range keeps the
  # list's own style, which drops the leading digits a last page shares with the first.
  19, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "A page range printed as its first page alone, in Bullock, Green, and Ha (2010)",
  "p. 694, refs",
  "Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 98(4): [[550]].",
  "Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 98(4): [[550–58]].",
  str_c("The article runs from 550 to 558 (doi ",
        "[10.1037/a0018933](https://doi.org/10.1037/a0018933))."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  20, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "A page range printed as its first page alone, in Laplante and Theidon (2007)",
  "p. 695, refs",
  "Human Rights Quarterly 29: [[228]].",
  "Human Rights Quarterly 29: [[228–50]].",
  str_c("The article runs from 228 to 250 (doi ",
        "[10.1353/hrq.2007.0009](https://doi.org/10.1353/hrq.2007.0009))."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  21, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "A page range printed as its first page alone, in Rubin (1974)",
  "p. 695, refs",
  "Journal of Educational Psychology 66(5): [[688]].",
  "Journal of Educational Psychology 66(5): [[688–701]].",
  str_c("The article runs from 688 to 701 (doi ",
        "[10.1037/h0037350](https://doi.org/10.1037/h0037350))."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  # Entry 22 was found on 2026-11-11 while tabulating the democratization cases for a
  # reader: the switching-equation column table_b1_b2_case_dataset.R writes had flagged
  # both cases since August, and only Azerbaijan had been read.
  22, "float", "pipeline", "brief",
  "Two revealed untreated outcomes transposed in appendix Table B.2",
  "app. Table B.2",
  str_glue(
    "[[Azerbaijan (1991-1992) at a revealed untreated outcome of ",
    "{fmt0(revealed_az$observed_published)}, and Bangladesh (1982-1990) at ",
    "{fmt0(revealed_bd$observed_published)}]], in the $Y_i(0)$ column and again in the ",
    "$\\tilde{{Y}}_i(0)$ column"),
  str_glue(
    "[[Azerbaijan (1991-1992) at a revealed untreated outcome of ",
    "{fmt0(revealed_az$corrected_y0)}, and Bangladesh (1982-1990) at ",
    "{fmt0(revealed_bd$corrected_y0)}]], in the $Y_i(0)$ column and again in the ",
    "$\\tilde{{Y}}_i(0)$ column"),
  str_glue(
    "The article codes the outcome 1 when authoritarianism resumes within 10 years of the ",
    "transition. Polity IV, from which the case universe is drawn, records Azerbaijan's polity ",
    "score falling from 1 in 1992 to -3 in 1993, and Bangladesh's holding at 6 from 1991 through 2006 and falling only in ",
    "2007, seventeen years after its transition. The deposited `outcome` column records ",
    "{fmt0(revealed_az$corrected_y0)} and {fmt0(revealed_bd$corrected_y0)} accordingly. The ",
    "deposit's untreated potential outcome columns, which are what the analysis reads, carry ",
    "the two values transposed, and the table prints them as the deposit holds them. With ",
    "entry 11, the corrected Azerbaijan row reads 1 in all three columns. Both cases are left ",
    "unimputed, so each enters the analysis through this value alone, and because the two are ",
    "swapped the sum of the untreated outcomes is the same either way: no bound, figure, or ",
    "table in the article moves."),
  "",
  NA_character_) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values),
                as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one object, so they begin in agreement and
# this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span to
# another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its value.
# Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the counts
# line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and its
# spans outnumber its values. A count the sentence spells out is accepted in its spelled form.
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

in_span <- function(v, s) {
  str_detect(s, fixed(v)) ||
    (str_detect(v, "^[0-9]+$") && as.integer(v) %in% seq_len(25) &&
       str_detect(s, fixed(english_number(as.integer(v)))))
}

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values)) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, in_span))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) in_span(v, s)))))
  }
})

# The placement is written to the spine as values_in_spans, one logical per entry: TRUE
# when every corrected value is the token its sentence prints, NA for an entry with no
# values. The gate below stops on FALSE, because no entry here stores a value on the
# claim's scale rather than the sentence's.
entries <- entries |>
  left_join(transmute(quantified, entry, values_in_spans = value_placed), by = "entry")

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none may
# not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds. A note-form
# entry corrects nothing and carries NA even where its class is quantity, and an entry with
# no claim_ids has no claim to carry a value for.
has_ids <- !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & entries$claim_ids != ""
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" & has_ids])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$form == "note"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | has_ids)
)

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one. Entries whose corrected artifact is a float take the heading and the
# note from the spine and keep their bespoke body between the two.
emit_heading <- function(n, lead = "") {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n", sep = "")
  if (lead != "") cat("\n", lead, "\n", sep = "")
}

emit_note <- function(n) cat("\n", entries$note[entries$entry == n], "\n", sep = "")

emit <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ",
      str_remove(e$location, "^published, "), ":\n\n> ", bold(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

This note lists `r english_number(nrow(entries))` corrections to "Qualitative Imputation of Missing Potential Outcomes," published in *American Journal of Political Science* 66(3), doi [10.1111/ajps.12697](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12697). **None of them changes a conclusion of the article.** The extreme value bounds on the average treatment effect, which are the article's headline result, are unchanged at [`r sprintf("%.0f", exact_bound("Democratization", "ATE", "s4", "lower"))`, `r sprintf("%.0f", exact_bound("Democratization", "ATE", "s4", "upper"))`] with a width of `r sprintf("%.0f", ate_width_exact)` points, as are every number in the abstract, the expert survey comparison in Figure 4, Table 5, and every quantity in the end-of-conflict application in Appendix A. **One published quantity does move materially**: the average treatment effect on the treated, which the article summarizes as a `r att_published` percentage point effect and which is `r sprintf("%.1f", att_exact)` points once the imputation probabilities the article's own appendix C states are the ones the analysis uses.

Entries 12 to 21 are of a different kind from the eleven before them. Entries 12 to 18 are misspellings, a missing space, a missing full stop, and three defects in the reference list, and they are here because a corrected re-typesetting of the article was prepared, which meant reading every word of it and of its appendix against the published pages. That is a finer sieve than any pass over the analysis, and no error is too small to list. Entries 19 to 21 are reference page ranges printed as a first page alone, found by an audit that checks every entry in the reference list against Crossref.

The first two entries are transcription errors in the deposited case data, and entries 3, 4, 9, and 10 are their consequences. The imputed potential outcomes in this article are not measurements. They are qualitative judgments, set out case by case in appendix C with the reasoning behind each one, and the deposited `cases_clean.csv` is a transcription of those judgments. `r str_to_sentence(english_number(nrow(corrections)))` of its imputation probabilities do not match the probability the appendix C narrative for that case states. Correcting them restores what the article always said it was doing. Entry 22 is a third transcription error, in two observed outcomes rather than imputed ones, and it moves no quantity.

Every corrected value is computed at the time this document is rendered, from the deposited replication archive ([10.7910/DVN/2IVKXD](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/2IVKXD)) with those `r english_number(nrow(corrections))` probabilities restored and the two outcomes of entry 22 corrected. The bounds are computed exactly, where the deposited script estimates them by simulation. It is the same quantity by a different route rather than a different estimator: a bound is affine in the imputed potential outcomes, so the distribution the deposit draws from can be written down and averaged, and the two agree to within the error of the simulation. What computing it exactly changes is that a bound falling exactly halfway between two whole numbers is visible as such, rather than being settled by whichever side an unseeded draw happened to land on. The code supporting each correction is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_kaur_2022](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_kaur_2022). Bold marks the values that change; unbolded numbers are recomputed rather than copied, so a reader diffing published against corrected sees every quantity verified and not only the ones at issue.

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
# The spine's vocabularies are closed (cleanup of 2026-11-07): a value outside them is a
# typo, and the edition builders read these columns to shape every entry.
stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
